provenance.source: Income Tax Act 1947; IRAS individual income tax rates for YA 2024 onwards; CPF contribution rates from 1 January 2026; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Singapore
provenance.notes: The resident rate table was confirmed on 31 August 2026 as applying to YA 2026 and onwards. The CPF Ordinary Wage ceiling of SGD 8,000 a month from 1 January 2026 and the SGD 80,000 relief cap were read from secondary sources rather than from the CPF and IRAS tables directly.

omissions: Additional Wage (bonus) CPF is not computed separately; the app applies the Ordinary Wage ceiling to whatever you enter in each month.
CPF rates for employees over 55 differ and are not modelled.
Non-resident taxation (a flat 15% on employment income or the resident rates, whichever is higher) is out of scope.
Parent relief, grandparent caregiver relief, NSman relief, the working mother's child relief and the foreign maid levy relief are not modelled individually; use the general reliefs field.

scale.note: Applied to chargeable income, that is assessable income after all reliefs. The first SGD 20,000 is untaxed.

cpf.note: Employees aged 55 and below contribute 20% of Ordinary Wages up to a monthly ceiling of SGD 8,000. Compulsory employee CPF is fully relieved from tax, so it reduces both take-home pay and taxable income.

reliefs.note: Every relief you claim, CPF included, counts against a single overall cap of SGD 80,000 for the year of assessment.

regions.name: Singapore
regions.note: Singapore has no state or municipal income tax.

inputSchema.label: Gross salary (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross monthly pay. The CPF Ordinary Wage ceiling is monthly, so pay above SGD 8,000 in a month attracts no further employee CPF for that month.

inputSchema.label: Singapore citizen or permanent resident
inputSchema.help: CPF is compulsory for citizens and permanent residents. Foreign employees on work passes do not contribute to CPF and so get no CPF relief.

inputSchema.label: Other personal reliefs claimed
inputSchema.help: Course fees, qualifying child relief, parent relief, NSman relief, SRS contributions and so on, added together. The combined total of all reliefs including CPF is capped at SGD 80,000.

inputSchema.label: Donations to approved IPCs
inputSchema.help: Qualifying donations attract a deduction of 2.5 times the amount given, and that deduction sits outside the SGD 80,000 relief cap.
